frequency_question: How often do central banks execute targeted reserve ratio hikes when facing specific liquidity overhangs?
membership_rule: Includes instances where a major central bank explicitly implements a secondary or incremental reserve requirement tool on commercial banks; excludes general statutory reserve ratio changes made during routine monetary policy tightening cycles.

cases.name: PBoC Targeted Reserve Requirement Ratio Adjustments
Bank of Israel Excess Liquidity Absorption Measure
Central Bank of Brazil Compulsory Deposit Requirement

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major instances; representative of targeted liquidity absorption actions by central bank principals.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or unpublicized administrative liquidity tightening measures.
skeleton: Central bank liquidity management interventions across major emerging markets during surplus liquidity episodes, observed over 4 distinct policy actions.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 documented major emerging market episodes where central banks possessed both the statutory mandate and clear intent to absorb surplus liquidity via targeted reserve ratios.
validity_reason: Central bank frameworks for deploying reserve ratio tools remain stable over multi-year horizons.
